key_insight: MamaBench shows that medical LLMs can look strong on standard questions yet still fail on clinically similar counterfactual cases, revealing important hidden fragility.
clinical_relevance: For maternal and child health diagnosis, this matters because safe AI support depends on distinguishing near-identical presentations that require different interventions.
method: Built MamaBench with 434 expert-authored clinical narratives in 217 counterfactual pairs across 371 pathologies.
Introduced Bias Trap Rate (BTR) to measure failure on the counterfactual case after success on the base case.
Proposed Evidence-Anchored RAG (EA-RAG), using parameter extraction, coverage auditing, and contrastive sub-queries to improve retrieval relevance.
evidence_signal: Across eight configurations of four frontier LLMs, base accuracy overstated robust accuracy by 16–28 percentage points, and EA-RAG reached 20.3% BTR and 65.0% robust accuracy on Claude Sonnet 4.6.
watch_item: Even with EA-RAG, a residual ~20% BTR remains, so counterfactual robustness is still not reliable enough for deployment without further validation.
paper_title: MamaBench: Benchmarking LLM Robustness in Maternal and Child Health Diagnosis through Counterfactual Clinical Perturbation
